The *Kisāgotamītherīapadāna* is a Pali poetic narrative found within the *Therīapadāna* collection [SuttaCentral]. The text presents the legendary biography, past-life aspirations, and ultimate liberation of the senior nun (therī) Kisāgotamī [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral lists five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].

Within the Pali textual corpus, the work is closely integrated into the commentarial and verse literature [DharmaNexus]. In particular, nearly the entire text (§§1.1–33.2) is shared with the commentary on the *Therīgāthā* (*Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*), with further overlapping passages appearing in the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* and *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. As is characteristic of the Apadāna genre, substantial formulaic verse sequences are shared across neighboring poems in the collection, showing extensive mutual text reuse with the *Dhammadinnātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 23), *Paṭācārātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 20), *Kuṇḍalakesātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 21), *Khemātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 18), and *Uppalavaṇṇātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 19) [DharmaNexus].
